          Newcastle vs Everton Prediction: Premier League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Nov 1, 2026
          
                      Chirag Sharatkumar / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Four days after a dominant EFL Cup victory, David Moyes' side will once again look to get the better of the Magpies. We look ahead to Monday's Premier League clash with our Newcastle vs Everton prediction and preview.
David Moyes will hope his Everton side can replicate their superb EFL Cup performance when they travel to St. James' Park to face Newcastle United again on Monday.

Everton booked their place in the EFL Cup quarter-finals on Thursday with a 3-1 victory over the Magpies at Hill Dickinson Stadium, with James Garner, Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry all finding the net.
While that result will undoubtedly boost their confidence, the Toffees have not quite managed to display the same fluency in the Premier League.
They have lost their last two league matches, including a 2-0 defeat at Arsenal last weekend, having last suffered three straight losses in January 2025.
Everton have not lost three on the trot under Moyes since October 2011, and the Scot will be desperate to keep it that way, but their recent away form does not inspire much confidence.

Since a dramatic 3-2 win on Tyneside in February, the Toffees are winless in all nine of their away Premier League matches (D5 L4), their worst run since going 14 without victory on the road between December 2023 and September 2024.
Newcastle, meanwhile, will be looking to make swift amends for Thursday's EFL Cup elimination.

Matthias Jaissle's side had already suffered a blip with back-to-back league defeats to Coventry City and Aston Villa, though they returned to winning ways with a confident 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace last weekend.
If Newcastle are to get revenge, sorting their leaky defence would go a long way.

Across the opening eight Premier League matchdays, Newcastle faced more shots than any other side (138), with those efforts amounting to an expected goals (xG) value of 13.7, the fourth-worst figure in the league.
It has been a persistent problem, with the Magpies facing at least 15 shots in six of those eight matches, the joint most of any team along with Coventry.

Everton's main concerns, meanwhile, also lie at the defensive end. The Toffees have made a habit of conceding the opening goal, going 1-0 down in 16 Premier League games in 2026, more often than every side bar Sunderland (18).
Indeed, Everton have won just one of their last 21 Premier League matches when conceding the opener (D7 L13), and none of their last 12 (D5 L7).

To address those issues, Moyes may turn to his Mr. Reliable, James Tarkowski, who remains vital as a stable defensive presence. The Everton captain has won more duels than any other player in the Premier League this season (63), while his 78% success rate is also the best of the 280 players to contest at least 20 duels.
Since making his first Premier League start for Burnley in 2017, Tarkowski leads all players in the competition for duels won (2,296), aerial duels won (1,398) and shots blocked (491).
For Newcastle, it's been Harvey Barnes – who is set to make his 100th Premier League appearance for the club on Monday – who has been delivering most consistently in the final third.
The 28-year-old has contributed to seven goals across his last 12 Premier League appearances (four goals, three assists), including five in his last six at St. James' Park (two goals, three assists).
Tino Livramento and Ewen Jaouen remain long-term absentees for Newcastle, though Jaissle could welcome back Matias Fernandez-Pardo and Lewis Miley for Monday's clash.

Moyes, meanwhile, was delighted to confirm Jarrad Branthwaite will return for the trip to Tyneside, though the big question over Jack Grealish‘s availability remains after the winger sat out the EFL Cup tie for breaching club protocols.
